exhibits.argument: Lifetime access is capped to a limited word allowance usable within 7 days.

exhibits.quote: *low word count threshold- the folks who would drop big bucks on this will get capped for total word counts
exhibits.argument: Buyer reports total word caps undermine unlimited lifetime access.

exhibits.quote: Pay once and get full access for life! It's cheaper than many of the yearly subscription prices you'd pay, and you'll get lifetime access + lifetime free updates.

trials.claim: All future Plan updates are included
trials.claimQuote: All future Wordplay - Long-Form AI Writer Plan updates
trials.reasoning: Two buyers report the tool is not updated anymore, remains static, and is stuck on AI versions 1 to 1.5 years old, contradicting included future updates in practice.

exhibits.quote: Not updated anymore. As a wrapper, the tool is quite decent. However, it only gives us access to old AI versions from 1 to 1.5 years ago.
exhibits.argument: Buyer reports the tool is not updated and stuck on old AI versions.

exhibits.quote: We have therefore invested at a specific point in time in a tool that unfortunately remains static and significantly behind in terms of text quality compared to what we get by freely prompting tools like ChatGPT, Claude, or Mistral most recent models.
exhibits.argument: Buyer reports the tool remains static and behind instead of receiving future updates.

exhibits.quote: Pay once and get full access for life! It's cheaper than many of the yearly subscription prices you'd pay, and you'll get lifetime access + lifetime free updates.
exhibits.argument: Vendor promises lifetime free updates as part of the one-time deal.

trials.claim: Can create 2,000+ words in one click
trials.claimQuote: The #1 Long-Form AI Writer. Create 2,000+ words in one click.
trials.reasoning: The vendor claims 5,000+ word articles and a buyer confirms producing 3,000-word posts. The prosecution quotes complain about repetition and total caps, not that 2,000+ words cannot be created.

exhibits.quote: a whole article with around 2500 words is in fact a whole some of repetitive blocks all saying the same things in different words.
exhibits.argument: Buyer reports long articles are just repetitive blocks saying the same thing.

exhibits.quote: *low word count threshold- the folks who would drop big bucks on this will get capped for total word counts
exhibits.argument: Buyer reports low word-count thresholds cap total output.

exhibits.quote: Wordplay helps you create 5,000+ word articles with minimal input and minimal edits required afterwards.
exhibits.argument: Vendor claims ability to create 5,000+ word articles which exceeds 2,000 words.

exhibits.quote: I can now produce my first three long-form blog posts (3000 words) in just under an hour.
exhibits.argument: Buyer confirms producing 3000-word long-form posts quickly with Wordplay.

trials.claim: Can add FAQs to win featured snippets on Google
trials.claimQuote: Optionally add FAQs to win featured snippets on Google
trials.reasoning: The vendor confirms an FAQ feature intended to give higher chances of winning featured snippets and to land in them. The prosecution only shows this is a chance, not a guaranteed win, which does not negate the feature.

exhibits.quote: We also have Google-friendly features like FAQs so that you have higher chances of winning featured snippets or showing
exhibits.argument: Vendor only promises higher chances, not winning featured snippets.

exhibits.quote: Does Google penalize websites that write blogs with an AI writer? This topic is widely debated and quite inconclusive.
exhibits.argument: Vendor admits Google outcome is inconclusive, undermining guaranteed snippet win.

exhibits.quote: We also have Google-friendly features like FAQs so that you have higher chances of winning featured snippets or showing up in the people also ask section on the search results page.
exhibits.argument: Vendor states its FAQ feature gives higher chances of winning featured snippets.

exhibits.quote: FAQ QuestionsAdd FAQs to your articles to make them longer & land in Google's featured snippets.
exhibits.argument: Vendor lists adding FAQs to land in Google's featured snippets as a feature.

trials.claim: Can import AI content directly into WordPress with plugin
trials.claimQuote: Import your AI content directly into WordPress with our Wordplay plugin
trials.reasoning: The vendor states content can be published with its WordPress plugin and a buyer confirms the plugin worked for them. The prosecution quote is a generic 404 definition and does not show the plugin fails.

exhibits.quote: The "404 Not Found" error is an HTTP status code that indicates that a web server could not find the resource requested by the client.
exhibits.argument: Buyer reports the WordPress plugin returns a 404 not found error.

exhibits.quote: Easily schedule & publish content with our WordPress plugin
exhibits.argument: Vendor states content can be scheduled and published with its WordPress plugin.

exhibits.quote: The Wordpress plugin sealed the deal for me, I'm upgrading already!
exhibits.argument: Buyer confirms the WordPress plugin works and was decisive for purchase.
